Chouzhou Bank appeared repeatedly throughout the documents, providing a detailed example of the role that correspondent services play in sanctions evasion. 时报审阅的许多文件来自总部位于莫斯科的金融服务公司 A7 。黑客在网上发布了该公司2025年初的大量记录。此外，时报还获取并分析了数千笔商业交易和其他文件，这些来自该公司在网上未受保护的内部数据库。稠行在文件中反复出现，为代理行服务在制裁规避中所起的作用提供了一个详细例证。 A7 did not respond to a request for comment. The Times reported last month that A7 helps Russian businesses evade economic restrictions by sending money abroad to buy goods, often through shell companies that have little purpose other than to mask such purchases. A7未回应置评请求。 时报上个月报道 ，A7通过将资金汇往国外购买商品，帮助俄罗斯企业规避经济限制，通常是通过除了掩盖此类采购外别无其他目的的空壳公司。 One shell company working on behalf of A7 in Kyrgyzstan made more than $10 million of restricted purchases during that period through a bank that held an account at Chouzhou. 通过一家在稠行持有账户的银行，一家在吉尔吉斯斯坦代表A7工作的空壳公司在此期间进行了超过1000万美元的受限采购。 In other instances, Russian companies bought industrial goods, including precision grinding machines that could be used to manufacturer components for weapons. 还有一些俄罗斯公司购买了工业产品，包括可用于制造武器部件的精密磨床。 In January 2025, transaction documents show, a Russian company bought $73,000 of components used to build electronic warfare systems. The parts were supplied by a Hong Kong distributor with a history of sales to Russian buyers, according to trade data. 交易文件显示，2025年1月，一家俄罗斯公司购买了价值7.3万美元的组件，用于制造电子战系统。贸易数据显示，这些部件由一家有向俄罗斯买家销售历史的香港分销商供应。 To complete the sale, First Abu Dhabi Bank, an Emirati bank, arranged to have the money sent to Chouzhou’s account at Bank of America. 为完成这笔交易，阿联酋的第一阿布扎比银行安排将资金汇至稠行在美国银行的账户。 As is standard practice in correspondent transactions, Bank of America received money transfer orders, but not details about the purchase itself. That allowed the nature of the goods, and who was buying them, to be obscured as the sale worked its way through the international banking system. 按照代理行交易的标准做法，美国银行收到了汇款指令，但不会得到有关采购本身的细节。这使得货物的性质以及买家的身份在交易通过国际银行系统进行时得以被掩盖。 Without explanation in June 2025, Bank of America ended its relationship with Chouzhou Bank, closing Account 0252, whose existence was disclosed on a Kyrgyz bank website. Chouzhou has continued to provide access to the dollar — through Citibank, JPMorgan Chase and Standard Chartered — for dozens of banks that otherwise lack direct access to the U.S. financial system, including in countries that have close economic ties to Russia, The Times found. 2025年6月，美国银行在没有解释的情况下终止了与稠行的关系，关闭了0252账户。该账户的存在曾在一家吉尔吉斯斯坦银行网站上披露。时报发现，稠行继续通过花旗银行、摩根大通和渣打银行为数十家原本无法直接进入美国金融系统的银行提供美元通道，其中包括与俄罗斯有密切经济联系的国家。 Chouzhou did not respond to detailed requests for comment. Reached in person at a banking conference in Miami in late September, a manager for the bank’s correspondent banking division declined to comment. 稠行未回应详细的置评请求。9月下旬在迈阿密举行的一次银行业会议上，本报得以面见该行代理行部门的一位经理，对方拒绝置评。 Representatives from Bank of America, Citigroup, Standard Chartered and First Abu Dhabi all said that they worked closely with law enforcement officials and governments. The representatives added that their banks regularly monitored correspondent activity and reported suspicious activity to the authorities in order to identify and help disrupt illicit banking networks. 美国银行、花旗集团、渣打银行和第一阿布扎比银行的代表均表示，他们与执法官员和政府密切合作。这些代表补充说，他们的银行定期监控代理行活动，并向当局报告可疑活动，以识别并帮助破坏非法银行网络。 While a spokeswoman for Citi and a spokesman for First Abu Dhabi said they would not comment on specific customers, all four banks emphasized that they maintained rigorous internal controls to combat money laundering, sanctions evasion and other financial crimes. JPMorgan declined to comment. 尽管花旗和第一阿布扎比的发言人都表示不会对特定客户置评，但四家银行均强调，他们保持着严格的内部控制，以打击洗钱、制裁规避和其他金融犯罪。摩根大通拒绝置评。 An essential piece of plumbing 必不可少的基础设施 The correspondent banking system is an opaque and antiquated yet essential piece of financial plumbing that underpins international finance. It has played a crucial role in making the dollar the dominant currency for international trade and giving the United States unmatched leverage over financial transactions. 作为国际金融的支柱，代理行系统是一个不透明且陈旧但又必不可少的金融管道。它在使美元成为国际贸易主导货币以及赋予美国在金融交易中无可比拟的影响力方面发挥了至关重要的作用。 Here’s how it works: Imagine that a fabric exporter in rural China wants to sell its goods to customers abroad. It would be impractical for the exporter, or even its local bank, to maintain accounts in every country and in every currency that its customers might want to use. 其运作方式如下：想象一下，中国农村的一家面料出口商想向海外客户出售商品。对于该出口商，甚至其当地银行来说，在客户可能想要使用的每个国家和每种货币中维护账户是不切实际的。 Correspondent banking solves this problem. The exporter’s local Chinese bank holds dollar, euro and other currency accounts at a select few global banks. Through those accounts, the Chinese bank gains access to the broad networks of those international banks, allowing its customers to send and receive international payments and convert proceeds into local currencies. 代理行解决了这个问题。出口商的当地中资银行在少数全球银行持有美元、欧元和其他货币账户。通过这些账户，中资银行获得了这些国际银行的广泛网络，使其客户能够收发国际支付，并将收益兑换成本地货币。 By its nature, however, the correspondent system can add distance between big banks and small companies seeking to circumvent their controls. Big banks often delegate the vetting of customers and transactions to smaller banks further down the correspondent chain. 然而，代理行系统本质上会在大银行与试图规避其控制的小公司之间增加距离。大银行通常将客户和交易的审查委托给代理链下游的小银行。 When new regulations were put in place to stop terror financing after the Sept. 11, 2001, attacks, banks began cutting correspondent relationships around the globe. 2001年9月11日袭击后为阻断恐怖主义资金渠道而实施了新规，银行随即开始在全球范围内削减代理行关系。 Sudan, which the United States labeled a state sponsor of terrorism, was hit especially hard. Many banks stopped handling payments from the country, raising fears that it could be cut off from the global financial system and pushed toward shadow banking networks in order to supply its citizens with even basic necessities. 被美国列为支持恐怖主义国家的苏丹受到的打击尤其严重。许多银行停止处理来自该国的付款，引发其被隔绝于全球金融体系之外的担忧，哪怕国民的最基本需求都被迫要转向影子银行网络。 Since then, regulators have tried to balance the risk of sanctions evasion with the goal of keeping the dollar used around the world. In 2016, the Treasury Department issued guidance that said banks did not need to individually vet their correspondent’s clients, a practice called “know your customer’s customer.” 自那以后，监管机构一直试图在制裁规避风险与保持美元在全球使用这一目标之间取得平衡。2016年，美国财政部发布指引称，银行无需逐一审查其代理行客户——也就是所谓“了解你的客户的客户”的原则。 When transactions pass through an American bank, the Treasury Department has broad jurisdiction to regulate and police the activity. Last month, for example, the U.S. government issued economic restrictions against two foreign banks that used the correspondent system to help Iran gain access to the dollar system in order to launder money and evade sanctions on behalf of the Islamic Revolutionary Guards Corps. 当交易通过美国银行时，美国财政部拥有广泛的管辖权来监管和监督该活动。例如，上个月，美国政府对外国银行实施经济限制，这两家银行利用代理行系统帮助伊朗进入美元体系，以便为伊斯兰革命卫队洗钱和规避制裁。 U.S. banks can face legal liability for processing restricted transactions even when acting only as a correspondent for another financial institution. However, the Treasury Department has discretion over the cases it pursues. 即使仅作为另一家金融机构的代理行处理受限交易，美国银行也可能面临法律责任。然而，美国财政部对追查哪些案件拥有自由裁量权。 Depending on the extent of the illicit activity and the level of the bank’s due diligence, it would be difficult to imagine an American bank being penalized for unwittingly playing a role in a sophisticated sanctions evasion scheme, according to a former senior Treasury official who was not authorized to speak publicly about enforcement procedures. 据一位未获授权公开谈论执法程序的前财政部高级官员称，很难想象一家美国银行会因在复杂的制裁规避计划中无意中发挥作用而受到处罚，具体要看非法活动的情节和银行尽职调查的水平。 A critical lifeline 一条关键的生命线 Chouzhou was founded in Yiwu in 1987 and grew as the midsize Chinese trading city blossomed into a manufacturing hub for goods that are sent around the world. 稠州商业银行于1987年在义乌成立，随着这座中国中型贸易城市发展成为向世界各地输送商品的制造业中心而成长。 Over the years, it carved out a niche by offering correspondent services to dozens of banks in countries identified by Western officials as high risk for money laundering or sanctions evasion, including Afghanistan, Yemen and South Sudan, according to the documents obtained by The Times and data from BankCheck, a correspondent banking compliance platform. 据时报获得的文件以及代理行合规平台BankCheck的数据，多年来，通过向西方官员认定为洗钱或制裁规避高风险的数十个国家的银行提供代理行服务，这家银行开辟了一个利基市场，这些国家包括阿富汗、也门和南苏丹。 Chouzhou has an especially large presence in Kyrgyzstan, Georgia and Uzbekistan — countries with close economic ties to Russia that have become important hubs for rerouted trade. 稠行在吉尔吉斯斯坦、格鲁吉亚和乌兹别克斯坦尤其活跃，这些国家与俄罗斯有密切经济联系，已成为改道贸易的重要枢纽。 According to the BankCheck data, Chouzhou provides access to dollar accounts to nearly 70 other banks, most of which otherwise lack direct access to the U.S. financial system. Those banks, in turn, market dollar accounts to their customers. 根据BankCheck数据，稠行为近70家其他银行提供美元账户通道，其中大多数原本无法直接进入美国金融系统。这些银行反过来又向客户推销美元账户。 By comparison, Industrial and Commercial Bank of China, the largest bank in the world by assets, provides dollar access to 20 banks. HSBC Bank in London provides just seven dollar correspondent accounts to other banks, BankCheck data shows. 相比之下，按资产计全球最大的银行中国工商银行为20家银行提供美元通道。BankCheck数据显示，伦敦的汇丰银行仅向其他银行提供七个美元代理账户。 In 2024, Chouzhou processed more than $200 billion in international transactions, according to a bond prospectus, nearly four times the amount of its total assets. But that is likely a small fraction of its activity now: At the financial services conference in Miami last month, Chouzhou advertised relationships with more than 1,000 banks and the ability to process payments in 27 currencies. 根据一份债券招股说明书，2024年，稠行处理了超过2000亿美元的国际交易，将近其总资产的四倍。但这可能只是其当前活动的一小部分：在上个月迈阿密的金融服务会议上，稠行宣传其与1000多家银行保持着关系，有能力处理27种货币支付。 Chouzhou stopped processing transactions directly with Russian and Belarusian banks in early 2024, according to news releases and trade documents. But it has continued working with customers and banks in countries considered high risk for Russian sanctions evasion. 据 新闻稿 和贸易文件，稠行于2024年初停止直接处理与俄罗斯和白俄罗斯银行的交易。但它继续与被视为俄罗斯制裁规避高风险国家的客户和银行合作。 Soon after Bank of America ended its relationship with Chouzhou last year, the Chinese bank opened two new dollar accounts at Citibank and Standard Chartered, BankCheck data shows. BankCheck数据显示，去年美国银行终止与稠行的关系后不久，这家中国银行在花旗银行和渣打银行开设了两个新的美元账户。 The accounts remain open. 这些账户至今仍正常使用。 翻译：纽约时报中文网 点击查看本文英文版。 获取更多RSS： https://feedx.net https://feedx.site

items.title: 鼠疫疑云超一周，俄罗斯仍未作出官方解释
items.description: PAUL SONNE, JULIAN E. BARNES2026年10月12日位于俄罗斯伊尔库茨克的西伯利亚及远东地区抗鼠疫研究所，摄于周三。该所一名28岁研究人员死于不明原因的肺炎。” Associated Press More than a week after a young plague researcher’s mysterious death from pneumonia, Russia has still not publicly identified the pathogen that killed her. 一名年轻的鼠疫研究人员因肺炎神秘死亡已超过一周，俄罗斯至今仍未公开确认导致她死亡的病原体。 The possibility that the researcher contracted pneumonic plague in her lab led to global fears of an outbreak. Those worries have begun to recede as no other known cases have surfaced in the Irkutsk region, where Darya Shipilova, a 28-year-old researcher at the Anti-Plague Institute of Siberia and the Far East, died on Oct. 2. 由于这名研究人员可能是在实验室感染肺鼠疫的，这引发了全球对疫情暴发的担忧。不过，随着伊尔库茨克地区未出现其他已知病例，这种担忧已经开始消退。10月2日，28岁的达里娅·希皮洛娃在该地区去世。她生前是西伯利亚及远东地区抗鼠疫研究所的一名研究人员。 But the absence of an official explanation for Ms. Shipilova’s death, despite thousands of tests conducted on others in the community and on her own remains, has stoked concerns about what, if anything, Russia’s authoritarian government might be hiding. 然而，尽管当局对当地其他居民以及希皮洛娃的遗体进行了数千次检测，却始终未对她的死因给出官方解释，这不禁令人怀疑，俄罗斯威权政府是否有所隐瞒，如果确实如此，它究竟在隐瞒什么？ According to Rospotrebnadzor, the Russian public health regulator, Ms. Shipilova’s remains did not test positive for any of the dangerous pathogens she was working on at the institute, which included the bacterium that causes the plague. The regulator has said she died of pneumonia of an unknown origin. Pneumonia can be caused by numerous viruses, bacteria and fungi. 据俄罗斯公共卫生监管机构——联邦消费者权益保护和公益监督局称，希皮洛娃的遗体没有检测出她在研究所接触的任何危险病原体呈阳性，其中包括引起鼠疫的细菌。该监管机构说，她死于来源不明的肺炎。肺炎可由多种病毒、细菌和真菌引起。 The World Health Organization is still seeking to understand the “causative agent” of the fatal pneumonia, whether or not it was the plague, Maria Van Kerkhove, the W.H.O.’s director of epidemic and pandemic management, said at a news conference on Wednesday. 世界卫生组织负责流行病和大流行病管理的主任玛丽亚·范凯尔克霍夫周三在新闻发布会上表示，世卫组织仍在设法查明这起致命肺炎病例的“致病因子”，包括确认它是否由鼠疫引起。 “If that is ruled out — they say that is ruled out — what did she actually die from?” Ms. Van Kerkhove asked. “如果鼠疫的可能性被排除了——他们说已经排除了——那么她究竟是因为什么死的？”范凯尔克霍夫问道。 Experts said they believed that with modern testing technology, the Russian authorities should know the answer by now. 专家表示，他们认为，凭借现代检测技术，俄罗斯当局现在应该已经知道答案。 “Presumably, they have the capability within days to do a simple genome sequence,” said Raj Panjabi, who served as a White House public health official during the Biden administration. “Presumably, they’ve done that, but they’ve not shared the results, and that’s concerning.” “按理说，他们有能力在几天内完成简单的基因组测序，”拜登政府时期曾担任白宫公共卫生官员的拉杰·潘贾比说。“按理说，他们已经做了测序，但没有公布结果，这令人担忧。” The lingering questions reflect a broader lack of global public trust that stems in part from unanswered questions about the origins of the Covid-19 pandemic. 这些挥之不去的疑问反映出全球公众普遍存在的信任缺失，而这种不信任在一定程度上源于新冠疫情的起源至今仍未得到解答。 More than six years after Covid upended the world, questions remain about whether the lab that was studying bat coronaviruses in the Chinese city where the pandemic started played a role in the outbreak. China swiftly rejected the possibility and impeded a global investigation into the matter. 新冠疫情给世界带来巨大冲击，六年多过去了，人们仍有诸多疑问尚未得到解答，其中包括：在疫情最初暴发的那座中国城市，一家从事蝙蝠冠状病毒研究的实验室是否与疫情暴发有关。中国迅速否认了这种可能性，并阻碍国际社会对此展开调查。 In Russia, any possible case of a pathogen escaping a lab attracts outsize attention globally in part because the country is one of the few in the world that continues to work on biological weapons, according to the U.S. intelligence community’s annual threat assessment. 在俄罗斯，任何一起疑似病原体从实验室泄漏的事件都会引起国际社会的高度关注。部分原因是，根据美国情报界的年度威胁评估，俄罗斯是世界上少数几个仍在开展生物武器研究的国家之一。 That has led to greater concern among officials and experts in the United States, who point to the nation’s vulnerabilities. 这加剧了美国官员和专家的担忧，他们指出，美国在应对这类威胁方面存在薄弱环节。 “The United States does not have a licensed plague vaccine,” said Andrew Weber, a senior fellow at the Council on Strategic Risks and a former Pentagon official in charge of biodefense. “Given that Russia has an illegal bioweapons program, it is very concerning.” “美国没有获得许可的鼠疫疫苗，”战略风险委员会高级研究员、曾在五角大楼负责生物防御事务的安德鲁·韦伯说。“鉴于俄罗斯有一个非法生物武器项目，这非常令人担忧。” There is no indication that the Irkutsk institute was doing bioweapons research, people briefed on U.S. intelligence said, speaking on the condition of anonymity to give a candid assessment. 听取过美国情报简报的人士表示，没有迹象表明伊尔库茨克的这家研究所正在开展生物武器研究。这些人士要求匿名，以便坦率地作出评估。 Ms. Shipilova was involved in testing which antibiotics and doses worked against Y. pestis, the bacterium that causes the plague, according to the summary of a study presented this year at a Moscow infectious disease conference. 根据今年在莫斯科一场传染病会议上发表的研究摘要，希皮洛娃参与了针对鼠疫耶尔森菌的研究，测试哪些抗生素及多大剂量能够有效对抗这种引发鼠疫的细菌。 The plague, which is endemic to Siberia and some other regions of the world, caused the “Black Death” that ravaged Eurasia in the 14th century, but it is treatable with antibiotics if caught quickly. Pneumonic plague is considered the most dangerous of the three main forms of infection, because it spreads from person to person and causes deadly, rapid-onset pneumonia. 鼠疫在西伯利亚和世界其他一些地区属于地方性流行病。14世纪肆虐欧亚大陆的“黑死病”就是由鼠疫引起的，但如果及早发现，可用抗生素治疗。肺鼠疫被认为是鼠疫三种主要感染类型中最危险的一种，因为它可以在人与人之间传播，并迅速引发致命性肺炎。 Referring to Ms. Shipilova as “the patient,” the Russian authorities have said that she was vaccinated against the dangerous microorganisms she was working with, and that two reviews of the institute ruled out any “emergency situations” at the lab. The quarantine measures that the Russian authorities took in the Irkutsk region were put in place out of caution, owing to the nature of the patient’s work, they said. 俄罗斯当局将希皮洛娃称为“患者”，并表示她已经接种了针对其工作中接触的危险微生物的疫苗，对研究所进行的两次调查也排除了实验室存在任何“紧急情况”。他们说，之所以在伊尔库茨克地区采取隔离措施，是考虑到患者的工作性质，出于谨慎而采取的预防措施。 Plague vaccines have long existed, but experts have raised serious doubts about their effectiveness and safety. 鼠疫疫苗早已问世，但专家对其有效性和安全性一直存在严重质疑。 Beyond what pathogen led to Ms. Shipilova’s pneumonia, many other questions remain unanswered, including where she was in the days leading up to her death, what she was working on at the institute at the time, and how and when her illness first showed itself and then progressed. 除了是什么病原体导致希皮洛娃患上肺炎之外，还有许多问题没有答案，包括她去世前几天在哪里、当时在研究所做什么，以及她的病症最初何时出现、有哪些表现，之后又是如何发展的。 Labs around the world working with deadly germs take extensive precautions to keep workers from being infected, but accidents have occurred. 世界各地研究致命病原体的实验室都会采取严格的防护措施，避免工作人员受到感染，但事故仍有发生。 Though Russia took swift action to quarantine and test individuals who had come into contact with the researcher, Rospotrebnadzor has not held any news briefings and has provided information only in periodic public statements. The Kremlin has declined to field specific questions, urging the public to listen only to public health officials. 尽管俄罗斯迅速采取行动，对与这名研究人员有过接触的人实施隔离和检测，但俄联邦消费者权益保护和公益监督局没有举行过任何新闻发布会，只是不定期发布公开声明。克里姆林宫则拒绝回答具体问题，敦促公众只听取公共卫生官员发布的信息。 Russia has been slow to reveal the details of other incidents with possible public health implications. 对于其他可能影响公众健康的事件，俄罗斯也曾迟迟不肯披露相关细节。 In 2019, Moscow concealed critical information about the failed underwater recovery of a nuclear-powered missile in the White Sea, which caused an explosion and left seven people dead. The authorities did not initially say that a nuclear device was involved, acknowledge a spike in radiation or warn doctors that they were treating irradiated patients. 2019年，俄罗斯在白海打捞一枚核动力导弹失败，引发爆炸，造成七人死亡。莫斯科隐瞒了这一事件的关键信息。俄罗斯当局最初既没有说明事件涉及核装置，也没有承认辐射水平曾急剧上升，更没有提醒医生，他们正在救治的患者受到了辐射。 Nondisclosure has long been the modus operandi of the Soviet and now Russian bureaucracy, said Alexander Kelle, a senior researcher at the Institute for Peace Research and Security Policy at the University of Hamburg in Germany. He cautioned against reading too much into the paucity of details. 德国汉堡大学和平研究与安全政策研究所高级研究员亚历山大·凯勒表示，不披露信息长期以来一直是苏联乃至如今俄罗斯官僚机构的惯常做法。他提醒人们，不要因为披露的细节有限就过度解读。 “Just because there is a lack of information, we have to be careful not to equate that with something nefarious,” Mr. Kelle said, noting that there were many legitimate public health reasons for researchers to work on dangerous pathogens. “正因为信息缺乏，我们就必须谨慎，不能因此认定背后有什么不可告人的勾当，”凯勒说，并指出研究人员研究危险病原体有许多正当的公共卫生理由。 To posit any link to Russian biowarfare, he said, would “be stretching the very limited evidence that has been presented too far.” 他说，如果据此推断这起事件与俄罗斯的生物战研究存在任何联系，那就“远远超出了目前极其有限的证据所能支持的范围”。 In a video message on Thursday, the governor of the Irkutsk region, Igor Kobzev, sought to close the book on the episode. He said that the medical monitoring of people in the region had concluded and thanked his fellow Russian officials for taking swift action under intense scrutiny. 伊尔库茨克州州长伊戈尔·科布泽夫周四发布视频讲话，试图为这一事件画上句号。他说，对该地区相关人员的医学监测已经结束，并感谢俄罗斯其他官员在受到密切关注的情况下迅速采取行动。 Mr. Kobzev said the W.H.O. had publicly confirmed that there were no risks to public health, though the organization has said it has not received enough information from Russia to make a risk assessment. 科布泽夫称，世卫组织已公开确认不存在公共卫生风险。然而，世卫组织表示，尚未从俄罗斯获得足够的信息，无法进行风险评估。 Some people commenting on Mr. Kobzev’s video in his Telegram channel weren’t having it. 但在科布泽夫的Telegram频道上，一些给他的视频留言的人并不买账。 “What caused the pneumonia that killed the healthy young woman?” one asked. “究竟是什么引发了肺炎，夺走了这名健康年轻女性的生命？”一人问道。 “Are there really still naïve, gullible people in our city who would believe this?” another commenter said. 另一名评论者说：“难道我们这座城市里真的还有这么天真、这么轻信别人的人，会相信这一套吗？” A third wrote: “X-Files, nothing to see here.” 还有人写道：“简直就是《X档案》：没什么好看的，都散了吧。” K. R. Callaway对本文有报道贡献。 Paul Sonne是一名国际新闻记者，报道俄罗斯新闻和普京的国内和国际政策产生的一系列影响，主要关注乌克兰战争。 Julian E. Barnes为《纽约时报》报道美国情报机构和国际安全事务。他撰写安全相关议题已有20余年。 翻译：纽约时报中文网 点击查看本文英文版。

BARNES 2026年10月12日 位于俄罗斯伊尔库茨克的西伯利亚及远东地区抗鼠疫研究所，摄于周三。该所一名28岁研究人员死于不明原因的肺炎。” Associated Press More than a week after a young plague researcher’s mysterious death from pneumonia, Russia has still not publicly identified the pathogen that killed her. 一名年轻的鼠疫研究人员因肺炎神秘死亡已超过一周，俄罗斯至今仍未公开确认导致她死亡的病原体。 The possibility that the researcher contracted pneumonic plague in her lab led to global fears of an outbreak. Those worries have begun to recede as no other known cases have surfaced in the Irkutsk region, where Darya Shipilova, a 28-year-old researcher at the Anti-Plague Institute of Siberia and the Far East, died on Oct. 2. 由于这名研究人员可能是在实验室感染肺鼠疫的，这引发了全球对疫情暴发的担忧。不过，随着伊尔库茨克地区未出现其他已知病例，这种担忧已经开始消退。10月2日，28岁的达里娅·希皮洛娃在该地区去世。她生前是西伯利亚及远东地区抗鼠疫研究所的一名研究人员。 But the absence of an official explanation for Ms. Shipilova’s death, despite thousands of tests conducted on others in the community and on her own remains, has stoked concerns about what, if anything, Russia’s authoritarian government might be hiding. 然而，尽管当局对当地其他居民以及希皮洛娃的遗体进行了数千次检测，却始终未对她的死因给出官方解释，这不禁令人怀疑，俄罗斯威权政府是否有所隐瞒，如果确实如此，它究竟在隐瞒什么？ According to Rospotrebnadzor, the Russian public health regulator, Ms. Shipilova’s remains did not test positive for any of the dangerous pathogens she was working on at the institute, which included the bacterium that causes the plague. The regulator has said she died of pneumonia of an unknown origin. Pneumonia can be caused by numerous viruses, bacteria and fungi. 据俄罗斯公共卫生监管机构——联邦消费者权益保护和公益监督局称，希皮洛娃的遗体没有检测出她在研究所接触的任何危险病原体呈阳性，其中包括引起鼠疫的细菌。该监管机构说，她死于来源不明的肺炎。肺炎可由多种病毒、细菌和真菌引起。 The World Health Organization is still seeking to understand the “causative agent” of the fatal pneumonia, whether or not it was the plague, Maria Van Kerkhove, the W.H.O.’s director of epidemic and pandemic management, said at a news conference on Wednesday. 世界卫生组织负责流行病和大流行病管理的主任玛丽亚·范凯尔克霍夫周三在新闻发布会上表示，世卫组织仍在设法查明这起致命肺炎病例的“致病因子”，包括确认它是否由鼠疫引起。 “If that is ruled out — they say that is ruled out — what did she actually die from?” Ms. Van Kerkhove asked. “如果鼠疫的可能性被排除了——他们说已经排除了——那么她究竟是因为什么死的？”范凯尔克霍夫问道。 Experts said they believed that with modern testing technology, the Russian authorities should know the answer by now. 专家表示，他们认为，凭借现代检测技术，俄罗斯当局现在应该已经知道答案。 “Presumably, they have the capability within days to do a simple genome sequence,” said Raj Panjabi, who served as a White House public health official during the Biden administration. “Presumably, they’ve done that, but they’ve not shared the results, and that’s concerning.” “按理说，他们有能力在几天内完成简单的基因组测序，”拜登政府时期曾担任白宫公共卫生官员的拉杰·潘贾比说。“按理说，他们已经做了测序，但没有公布结果，这令人担忧。” The lingering questions reflect a broader lack of global public trust that stems in part from unanswered questions about the origins of the Covid-19 pandemic. 这些挥之不去的疑问反映出全球公众普遍存在的信任缺失，而这种不信任在一定程度上源于新冠疫情的起源至今仍未得到解答。 More than six years after Covid upended the world, questions remain about whether the lab that was studying bat coronaviruses in the Chinese city where the pandemic started played a role in the outbreak. items.title: 中欧就混动汽车贸易达成谅解，避免经贸摩擦升级
items.description: KEITH BRADSHER2026年10月12日欧盟委员会贸易和经济安全委员马罗什·谢夫乔维奇在北京出席记者会。 Kyodo, via Reuters Connect High-level talks in Beijing between the European Union and China ended on Friday with an unexpected agreement that could pull the two sides back from an imminent trade war. 欧盟与中国在北京举行的高级别会谈于周五结束，双方出人意料地达成一项协议，有望避免一场迫在眉睫的贸易战。 The most notable feature of the agreement involved what both sides described as an understanding on China’s exports of hybrid electric-gasoline cars, which have been among the most contentious points of tension between the two sides. 这项协议最引人注目的内容涉及中国出口的混动汽车。双方均表示，已就这一问题达成谅解。混动汽车一直是中欧贸易关系中最具争议的问题之一。 Maros Sefcovic, the trade commissioner of the 27-nation bloc, said that the understanding could lead to China’s halving the number of hybrid gasoline-electric cars that it sends to the European Union in the next four years. Neither side made any mention of any tariffs on those cars, which China has resolutely opposed. 欧盟委员会贸易和经济安全委员马罗什·谢夫乔维奇表示，根据双方达成的谅解，中国可能在未来四年内将出口欧盟的混动汽车数量削减一半。双方均未提及对这类汽车征收关税的问题，中国一直坚决反对加征关税。 China’s Ministry of Commerce said in a separate statement that the two sides had “reached an understanding on trade in hybrid vehicles in a manner consistent with World Trade Organization rules.” Complying with those rules makes it difficult for Europe to impose tariffs quickly. Tariffs also make it hard to know how many cars will continue to arrive from China, but Mr. Sefcovic said that the understanding would achieve specific reductions in imported cars. 中国商务部在另一份声明中说，双方“以符合世贸组织规则的方式就混动汽车贸易达成谅解”。遵守世贸组织规则意味着欧洲很难迅速加征关税。此外，即使征收关税，也难以确定还会有多少汽车继续从中国运来，但谢夫乔维奇表示，这项谅解将实现具体的进口汽车数量削减目标。 The compromise described by Mr. Sefcovic appeared to address the European Union’s need for immediate caps on the number of cars imported from China. It also addressed China’s need for an arrangement that would limit the often fierce competition among Chinese automakers in the European market, which has contributed to the Chinese automakers’ heavy losses. 谢夫乔维奇所描述的妥协方案似乎既满足了欧盟立即限制中国汽车进口数量的要求，也回应了中国希望通过某种安排缓解中国车企在欧洲市场激烈竞争的需求。这种竞争往往十分惨烈，也是造成中国汽车制造商巨额亏损的原因之一。 The agreement on hybrid cars appeared to have a strong resemblance to the two sides’ deal in 2013 for China to reduce the number of solar panels that it shipped each year to Europe, while Europe agreed to forgo its previous plans for tariffs on those shipments. This allowed Chinese solar panel makers to raise prices sharply in Europe for their limited supply of solar panels, producing large profits for Chinese solar panel manufacturers that previously were losing money. 这项关于混动汽车的协议似乎与双方2013年达成的太阳能电池板协议极为相似。当时，中国同意减少每年向欧洲出口的太阳能电池板数量，欧洲则同意放弃此前对这些产品加征关税的计划。这使中国太阳能电池板制造商得以大幅提高在欧洲市场的售价，凭借受到限制的供应量获得丰厚利润，扭转了此前的亏损局面。 The Chinese manufacturers invested those profits in more research and new factories, and now produce almost all of the world’s solar panels. 中国制造商随后将这些利润投入更多研发及新工厂的建设，如今几乎生产了全球所有的太阳能电池板。 China’s exports of plug-in hybrids to Europe have rapidly gained market share there and have contributed to Volkswagen’s recent plans to cut another 50,000 workers by the end of the decade, bringing its total reduction in its work force to 100,000. 中国出口欧洲的插电式混合动力汽车迅速扩大了在当地的市场份额，也是大众汽车最近计划在本十年结束前再裁员5万人、使其裁员总人数达到10万人的原因之一。 The European Union imposed tariffs of 7.8 to 35.3 percent on Chinese electric cars two years ago, on top of the region’s usual 10 percent tariff on imported cars. But the bloc did not impose extra tariffs then on plug-in hybrids. 两年前，欧盟在通常对进口汽车征收的10%关税基础上又对中国电动汽车征收7.8%至35.3%的关税。但欧盟当时没有对插电式混合动力汽车加征额外关税。 比亚迪电动车，2023年摄于慕尼黑。 China’s exports of plug-in hybrids have soared to almost 200,000 a month, from fewer than 10,000 a month, in just three years. Many are going to Europe. 短短三年间，中国插电式混合动力汽车出口从每月不足1万辆飙升至每月近20万辆，其中许多销往欧洲。 China has strenuously opposed the extra tariffs on its electric cars that the European Union imposed to limit the number of imports of these cars. Beijing has called for the tariffs on electric cars to be replaced instead with limits on the number of cars shipped. 中国一直强烈反对欧盟为限制中国电动汽车进口数量而对其加征的额外关税。北京方面主张应该取消这些关税，改为对汽车出口数量设定限制。 This would allow Chinese electric car manufacturers to raise prices and improve profitability — the arrangement for hybrid gasoline-electric cars that is now emerging. 这样一来，中国电动汽车制造商就能够提高售价，改善盈利能力。这也正是目前逐渐成形的混动汽车安排所采用的思路。 Asked on Friday whether the current agreement on hybrid cars resembled the solar panel deal, Mr. Sefcovic said that circumstances were different and that Europe needed immediate action on hybrid cars. “The public opinion and the leaders really expect very fast action from our side,” he said. 周五，当被问及目前的混动汽车协议是否与类似当年的太阳能电池板协议时，谢夫乔维奇说情况不同，而且欧洲需要立即采取行动应对混动汽车问题。他说：“公众舆论和领导人都确实期待我们迅速采取行动。” China has contended that unilateral tariffs are a violation of W.T.O. trade rules, which Beijing and the European Union are both still committed to uphold. By contrast, the Trump administration has repeatedly taken unilateral actions in defiance of W.T.O. norms. President Trump’s trade advisers have contended that China has a government-guided economy that does not follow the free market principles on which the W.T.O. was founded. 中国认为，单方面加征关税违反世界贸易组织的贸易规则，而北京和欧盟都仍然致力于维护这些规则。相比之下，特朗普政府一再采取违背世贸组织规则的单边行动。特朗普总统的贸易顾问声称，中国实行的是政府主导的经济体制，并不遵循世贸组织赖以创立的自由市场原则。 China’s Commerce Ministry dangled several carrots for the European Union to reach a compromise with Beijing. Mr. Sefcovic said that China had agreed to reduce tariffs on imports of European goods in categories like auto parts, olive oil and footwear with an annual value of almost 4 billion euros. 为促使欧盟与北京达成妥协，中国商务部提出了几项优惠措施。谢夫乔维奇表示，中国已同意降低汽车零部件、橄榄油和鞋类等欧洲商品的进口关税，这些商品的年贸易额接近40亿欧元。 This will save European exporters about €125 million a year in duties on their shipments to China, he said. 他说，这将使欧洲出口商每年向中国出口商品时节省约1.25亿欧元的关税。 A joint statement issued by China and the European Union was less specific, saying that “both sides will continue, within the framework of W.T.O. rules, to explore the possibility of tariff reductions or elimination for certain goods.” 中国与欧盟发表的联合声明则没有如此具体，只是表示，“双方将继续探讨在世贸组织规则框架下，降低部分商品关税的可能性。” Some issues were left unresolved, notably whether the European Union will also forgo plans to require that key components of technologies like electric cars and wind turbines be made in Europe. Also unresolved is whether the European Union will proceed with anti-subsidy tariffs on wind turbines. Mr. Sefcovic said that more talks were planned early next year. 一些问题仍未解决，尤其是欧盟是否会放弃要求电动汽车和风力涡轮机等技术产品的关键部件必须在欧洲制造的计划，以及欧盟是否仍将对风力涡轮机征收反补贴关税。谢夫乔维奇说，双方计划于明年初举行更多会谈。 Mr. Sefcovic is scheduled to return to Brussels on Saturday and brief officials ahead of a meeting of European presidents and prime ministers next week. 谢夫乔维奇定于周六返回布鲁塞尔，并将在下周欧洲各国领导人举行会议之前，向有关官员通报此次会谈的情况。 The first item on the agenda for the meeting of Europe’s leaders is how to handle the region’s weakening economic competitiveness — and trade with China is a central issue. European leaders have been warning of a hollowing out of Europe’s industrial base because of surging imports of manufactured goods from China. 欧洲领导人下周会议的首要议题是如何应对该地区经济竞争力不断减弱的问题，而对华贸易是其中的核心议题。欧洲领导人一直警告说，随着来自中国的制成品进口激增，欧洲的工业基础正面临被掏空的危险。 Time is on China’s side, with each passing month producing more than $30 billion in trade surplus for China and further weakening European competitors of Chinese manufacturers. 时间站在中国一边。每过去一个月，中国就能获得超过300亿美元的贸易顺差，并进一步削弱中国制造商的欧洲竞争对手。 China’s Commerce Ministry said in its statement that China would continue approving exports of rare earths and rare-earth magnets to Europe. China has restricted exports of rare earths and rare-earth magnets since April 2025 and has threatened further restrictions if Europe takes action against China’s exports. 中国商务部在声明中说，中国将继续批准对欧洲出口稀土和稀土磁体。自2025年4月以来，中国一直限制这两类产品的出口，并威胁如果欧洲对中国出口采取行动，将实施进一步限制。 The ministry also said that Europe had agreed to help resolve disputes over its export controls. 中国商务部还表示，欧盟已同意协助解决围绕其出口管制措施的争端。 Under pressure from President Joseph R. Biden Jr. and now President Trump, European companies have avoided selling to China the latest equipment used to make semiconductors with potential military applications. Beijing officials have contended that one of the fastest ways for Europe to narrow somewhat its trade deficit with China would be to sell the most advanced equipment regardless of American objections. 在前总统拜登以及现任总统特朗普的压力下，欧洲企业一直避免向中国出售最先进的半导体制造设备，因为这些设备生产的芯片可能被用于军事目的。北京官员认为，欧洲若想较快缩小对华贸易逆差，一个办法就是不顾美国反对，向中国出售最先进的设备。 Europe has also been preparing legislation to impose a made-in-Europe requirement for important components of products like electric cars or wind turbines. China used to have similar requirements for cars and wind turbines, but repealed them after years of complaints from Europe and other trading partners. Beijing now contends that Europe should not adopt such rules, which would force Chinese companies to invest in factories in Europe instead of exporting from factories at home, where their costs are often lower. 欧洲还一直在筹备立法，要求电动汽车或风力涡轮机等产品的重要零部件必须在欧洲制造。中国过去曾对汽车和风力涡轮机实施类似要求，但在欧洲和其他贸易伙伴多年抱怨后取消了这些规定。北京如今主张，欧洲不应出台这样的规定，因为这将迫使中国企业在欧洲投资建厂，而无法继续从生产成本通常更低的中国本土工厂向欧洲出口。 The Chinese statement said that China and the European Union had “agreed to explore investment cooperation to foster mutual economic development and to discuss future-oriented cooperation.” 中国商务部的声明称，中欧双方“同意探讨投资合作，促进彼此经济发展，并讨论开展面向未来的合作”。 Keith Bradsher是《纽约时报》北京分社社长，此前曾任上海分社社长、香港分社社长、底特律分社社长，以及华盛顿记者。他在新冠疫情期间常驻中国进行报道。 翻译：纽约时报中文网 点击查看本文英文版。

China has restricted exports of rare earths and rare-earth magnets since April 2025 and has threatened further restrictions if Europe takes action against China’s exports. 中国商务部在声明中说，中国将继续批准对欧洲出口 稀土 和稀土磁体。自2025年4月以来，中国一直限制这两类产品的出口，并威胁如果欧洲对中国出口采取行动，将实施进一步限制。 The ministry also said that Europe had agreed to help resolve disputes over its export controls. 中国商务部还表示，欧盟已同意协助解决围绕其出口管制措施的争端。 Under pressure from President Joseph R. Biden Jr. and now President Trump, European companies have avoided selling to China the latest equipment used to make semiconductors with potential military applications. Beijing officials have contended that one of the fastest ways for Europe to narrow somewhat its trade deficit with China would be to sell the most advanced equipment regardless of American objections. 在前总统拜登以及现任总统特朗普的压力下，欧洲企业一直避免向中国出售最先进的半导体制造设备，因为这些设备生产的芯片可能被用于军事目的。北京官员认为，欧洲若想较快缩小对华贸易逆差，一个办法就是不顾美国反对，向中国出售最先进的设备。 Europe has also been preparing legislation to impose a made-in-Europe requirement for important components of products like electric cars or wind turbines. China used to have similar requirements for cars and wind turbines, but repealed them after years of complaints from Europe and other trading partners. Beijing now contends that Europe should not adopt such rules, which would force Chinese companies to invest in factories in Europe instead of exporting from factories at home, where their costs are often lower. 欧洲还一直在筹备立法，要求电动汽车或风力涡轮机等产品的重要零部件必须在欧洲制造。中国过去曾对汽车和风力涡轮机实施类似要求，但在欧洲和其他贸易伙伴多年抱怨后取消了这些规定。北京如今主张，欧洲不应出台这样的规定，因为这将迫使中国企业在欧洲投资建厂，而无法继续从生产成本通常更低的中国本土工厂向欧洲出口。 The Chinese statement said that China and the European Union had “agreed to explore investment cooperation to foster mutual economic development and to discuss future-oriented cooperation.” 中国商务部的声明称，中欧双方“同意探讨投资合作，促进彼此经济发展，并讨论开展面向未来的合作”。 Keith Bradsher 是《纽约时报》北京分社社长，此前曾任上海分社社长、香港分社社长、底特律分社社长，以及华盛顿记者。他在新冠疫情期间常驻中国进行报道。 翻译：纽约时报中文网 点击查看本文英文版。

items.title: 美政府暂停微软等科技公司绿卡项目资格
items.description: ERICA L. GREEN2026年10月9日“我们要向微软传达的信息是：你们是一家伟大的美国公司，但你们必须雇用优秀的美国就业者，”副总统万斯周四在华盛顿表示。 Demetrius Freeman for The New York Times Vice President JD Vance announced on Thursday that Microsoft would be suspended from using a visa program that allowed foreign workers to permanently reside in the United States after an investigation found that the tech giant had “abused” the system. 副总统万斯周四宣布，在一项调查发现微软公司“滥用”允许外国员工获得美国永久居留权的签证项目后，政府将暂停微软使用该制度的资格。 Mr. Vance made the announcement in a news conference where he and other Trump administration officials made a slew of allegations that American companies and universities were committing visa fraud. Microsoft, they announced, is just the largest of several technology companies to face such a suspension, and schools including Harvard and Yale are now under investigation. 万斯在一场新闻发布会上宣布了这一决定。他和特朗普政府其他官员在会上提出了一系列指控，称美国企业和大学存在签证欺诈行为。他们宣布，微软只是面临此类暂停措施的多家科技公司中规模最大的一家，哈佛和耶鲁等高校目前也正在接受调查。 Mr. Vance took aim at the embattled H-1B visa program, which allows companies to hire skilled foreign workers in hard-to-fill jobs. The Trump administration has sought to overhaul the program, including imposing fees for the visas, claiming that it has unfairly allowed companies to sideline Americans and hire foreign workers. Mr. Vance has called the program “broken” and said he would support eliminating it. 万斯把矛头指向了饱受争议的H-1B签证项目。该项目允许公司为难以填补的岗位雇用外国高技能员工。特朗普政府一直试图改革这一计划，包括对签证收费，声称它不公平地让企业得以不公平地将美国人排除在外，转而雇用外国员工。万斯曾称该项目“已经失灵”，并表示支持取消它。 Mr. Vance said on Thursday that companies like Microsoft had been using the H-1B visa program to exploit the Labor Department’s permanent labor certification program, known as PERM, which allows H-1B visa recipients to obtain a green card and potentially stay in the United States indefinitely. 万斯周四说，微软等公司一直在利用H-1B签证项目，滥用劳工部的永久劳工认证项目(PERM)，该项目允许H-1B签证持有者获得绿卡，从而有可能无限期留在美国。 Officials said that other companies suspended from PERM would include Adobe and several large information technology outsourcing firms. Mr. Vance said the suspension would “last as long as it needs to.” 官员们表示，其他被暂停使用PERM项目的企业还包括Adobe和几家大型信息技术外包公司。万斯说，暂停措施将“持续到不需要为止”。 The announcement on Thursday, which included officials from several agencies, was the latest attempt by the administration to seize on purported fraud to argue that exploitation of the country’s immigration system — and not President Trump’s policies — has been depriving Americans of jobs, wages and paths to prosperity. 多个机构的官员出席了周四的发布会。这是本届政府最新一次试图利用所谓的欺诈行为来辩称，是美国移民制度的漏洞——而不是特朗普总统的政策——剥夺了美国人的工作、工资和致富之路。 “The Department of Labor is taking historic action by shutting down the pipeline of systemic fraud, the fraud that has flooded our country with foreign labor at the expense of American workers,” said Keith Sonderling, the labor secretary. “It begins with universities and companies that have turned into visa mills, promoting foreign workers that have lied about their qualifications to take jobs from our beloved American workers.” “劳工部正在采取历史性行动，切断系统性欺诈的渠道。正是这种欺诈让外国劳动力大量涌入我国，损害了美国就业者的利益，”劳工部长基思·桑德林说。“我们首先要针对那些沦为签证工厂的大学和企业。它们帮助谎报资历的外国员工获得签证，让他们抢走我们亲爱的美国就业者的工作。” But the administration has not always provided evidence to match its fraud claims. And several of its targets on Thursday disputed its assertions. 但特朗普政府提出欺诈指控时，并非总能拿出相应证据。周四被针对的几家机构也对政府的说法提出了异议。 Mr. Vance directed his harshest criticism at Microsoft, saying that there had been “no company in the United States, unfortunately, that has abused this system more.” 万斯对微软的批评最为严厉。他说，“遗憾的是，美国没有哪家公司比它更严重地滥用了这一制度”。 Mr. Vance said that in the past year, the company had laid off 6,000 American workers, while it benefited from 6,300 H-1B visas and nearly 3,000 green cards. He referred to the visa holders as “indentured servants” who were paid a fraction of what their American counterparts would be. 万斯说，过去一年，该公司裁掉了6000名美国就业者，同时却受益于6300份H-1B签证和近3000张绿卡。他把这些签证持有者称为“契约劳工”，说他们的薪酬远低于同等岗位的美国人。 “In other words, if you do the math, for every worker that Microsoft laid off, they replaced that worker with one and a half foreign indentured servants,” Mr. Vance said. “Now that is a scandalous system that we’ve allowed in this country for far too long.” “换句话说，你们可以算一算，微软每裁掉一名员工，就用一个半外国契约劳工来取代他，”万斯说。“这是一个可耻的制度，我们国家容忍它已经太久了。” “And so our message to Microsoft is: You’re a great American company, but you’ve got to hire great American workers,” he added. “You cannot lay off American workers and then replace them with foreign indentured servants.” “所以，我们要向微软传达的信息是：你们是一家伟大的美国公司，但你们必须雇用优秀的美国就业者，”他接着说。“你们不能先裁掉美国就业者，再用外国契约劳工取代他们。” In a statement, Microsoft challenged some of Mr. Vance’s claims. 微软在声明中反驳了万斯的部分说法。 The company said the “vast majority” of its employees in the United States are citizens. It said that of the roughly 6,000 H-1B applications it made last fiscal year, 80 percent were to extend or change the status of existing Microsoft employees. The remaining applications were for people already legally in the country who then joined Microsoft, the company said. 该公司表示，其在美国的员工“绝大多数”是美国公民。微软称，上一财年提交的约6000份H-1B签证申请中，80%是为了延长现有微软员工的签证有效期或变更其身份。公司表示，其余申请涉及的也是已经合法身在美国、随后加入微软的人员。 “They are not new arrivals to our country,” it added. “他们并不是新近来到我国的人，”微软补充道。 Microsoft said its pay is among the highest in tech and among H-1B filings. 微软表示，其薪酬水平在科技行业以及提交H-1B签证申请的企业中均位居前列。 “Microsoft succeeds as a global technology leader by developing the world’s best technology work force,” the company said. “We do this by strengthening this country’s talent pipeline, hiring American workers and attracting the best talent from around the world.” “微软之所以能够成为全球科技行业的领导者，是因为我们致力于打造世界一流的科技人才队伍，”该公司表示。“为此，我们不断加强美国本土的人才培养体系，雇用美国工人，同时吸引来自世界各地的顶尖人才。” On the academic front, Mr. Vance maintained that universities were employing foreign graduate students as research assistants at lower wages, and suggested that the visas were being overused and sucking up federal funding. 关于学界方面，万斯坚持认为，大学以较低工资雇用外国研究生担任研究助理，并暗示相关签证被过度使用，消耗了联邦资金。 Anthony D’Esposito, the inspector general of the Labor Department, announced that the agency was launching investigations into several universities for potential abuses of the J-1 visa, a cultural exchange program that allows foreign students to work and study in the United States. 劳工部监察长安东尼·德埃斯波西托宣布，该部门正对多所大学是否滥用J-1签证展开调查。这是一项文化交流签证计划，允许外国学生在美国工作和学习。 “Subpoenas have been served, investigations are underway, and nobody will be getting a free pass because their name is carved into an expensive building,” he said. “传票已经送达，调查正在进行，没有人会因为自己的名字刻在一栋昂贵的大楼上而获得特殊待遇，”他说。 The schools under investigation are Harvard, Yale, Stanford, Arizona State, Brown, M.I.T., the University of Pittsburgh, the University of California, Davis, and the California Institute of Technology. 接受调查的学校包括哈佛、耶鲁、斯坦福、亚利桑那州立、布朗、麻省理工、匹兹堡大学、加州大学戴维斯分校和加州理工。 Stanford said in a statement that it “complies with all applicable visa laws, including those relating to J-1 visas,” and “will cooperate with the investigation.” 斯坦福在声明中说，该校“遵守所有适用的签证法律，包括与J-1签证相关的法律”，并将“配合调查”。 Brian Clark, a spokesman for Brown University, said in a statement that the university had received the subpoena “for various records pertaining to foreign labor programs administered by the U.S. government, and we will respond promptly and directly.” 布朗大学发言人布莱恩·克拉克在声明中说，该校已收到传票，“要求提供与美国政府管理的外国就业者项目有关的各种记录，我们将迅速、直接地作出回应。” “Brown’s international scholars, students and employees make essential contributions on our campus, including to teaching and research that advances American innovation, competitiveness and economic vitality,” Mr. Clark said. “布朗大学的国际学者、学生和员工为我们的校园作出了不可或缺的贡献，包括通过教学和研究推动美国的创新、竞争力和经济活力，”克拉克说。 Arizona State University, noting that it educates more science, technology, engineering and math majors than any other university and employs one of the largest technical and scientific workforces in the country, said that it “has hired the talent needed to perform these functions and done so in complete compliance with existing United States policy and law.” 亚利桑那州立大学指出，该校培养的科学、技术、工程和数学专业学生人数超过美国其他大学，而且拥有全美规模最大的技术和科研人才队伍之一。该校表示，它“聘用了履行这些职能所需的人才，而且完全遵守美国现行政策和法律”。 The H-1B program has long been the target of bipartisan calls for changes, but has become a centerpiece of Mr. Trump’s immigration crackdown agenda. Economists have maintained that the visa holders boost American productivity and raise wages even for American workers. 长期以来，美国两党都呼吁改革H-1B签证计划，但如今它已成为特朗普收紧移民政策议程的核心内容之一。经济学家一直认为，H-1B签证持有人提高了美国的生产率，甚至能够提高美国就业者的工资。 Mr. Vance, pressed on how the use of the certification program amounted to fraud, said that companies were misrepresenting that they were bringing in workers with “hyper-specialized and hyper-capable” skill sets. 当被追问企业使用永久劳工认证制度为何构成欺诈时，万斯表示，企业虚假宣称自己引进的是拥有“高度专业化、能力超群”技能的人才。 Mr. Vance said that there was a difference between bringing in foreign workers like the tech tycoon Elon Musk, “who wants to come in and build something great in the United States of America,” versus an accountant at a lower wage. 万斯说，引进像科技大亨埃隆·马斯克这样“希望来到美利坚合众国成就一番伟业”的外国人才与雇用一名工资较低的会计师是两回事。 “You’re not bringing in a genius to build a great American corporation,” Mr. Vance said. “You are committing fraud against the American people and against this visa program.” “你引进的并不是一个能打造伟大美国企业的天才，”万斯说。“你是在欺骗美国人民，也是在欺骗这一签证项目。” Hours after the announcement, President Trump awarded Satya Nadella, Microsoft’s chief executive, the National Medal of Technology and Innovation at a summit in Washington where Mr. Musk and other tech executives also were honored. 就在这一消息宣布数小时后，特朗普总统在华盛顿举行的一场峰会上向微软首席执行官萨蒂亚·纳德拉颁发了国家技术与创新奖章。马斯克和其他科技企业高管也在会上受到表彰。 Mr. Nadella came to the United States for graduate school and joined Microsoft in 1992. Two years later, he wrote in his memoir, he turned in his permanent residency for an H-1B visa so that his wife could immediately join him in the United States. (At the time, he said, the spouses of green card holders faced a long wait for visa approval.) Both eventually gained citizenship, and he rose through the ranks to revive Microsoft from a yearslong slump. It is now worth almost $4 trillion. 纳德拉来美国读研究生，并于1992年加入微软。他在回忆录中写道，两年后，为了让妻子能够立即赴美与他团聚，他放弃了自己的永久居民身份，转而申请H-1B签证。（他说，当时绿卡持有人的配偶需要等待很长时间才能获得签证批准。）两人最终都获得了公民身份，而他也一路晋升，把微软从多年低迷中拯救出来。微软如今市值近4万亿美元。 In awarding Mr. Nadella the highest honor in technology on Thursday, Mr. Trump said it was “so well deserved,” and that Mr. Nadella had turned Microsoft into “an early leader in superintelligence.” 周四，特朗普向纳德拉颁发科技领域最高荣誉时表示，他“完全当之无愧”，并称纳德拉已将微软打造为“超级智能领域的早期领军者”。 Karen Weise自西雅图、Alan Blinder自亚特兰大、Vimal Patel自丹佛、Mark Arsenault自波士顿对本文有报道贡献。 Erica L. Green是时报白宫记者，报道特朗普总统及其政府。 翻译：纽约时报中文网 点击查看本文英文版。

The Trump administration has sought to overhaul the program , including imposing fees for the visas, claiming that it has unfairly allowed companies to sideline Americans and hire foreign workers. Mr. Vance has called the program “broken ” and said he would support eliminating it. 万斯把矛头指向了饱受争议的H-1B签证项目。该项目允许公司为难以填补的岗位雇用外国高技能员工。特朗普政府一直 试图改革这一计划 ，包括对签证收费，声称它不公平地让企业得以不公平地将美国人排除在外，转而雇用外国员工。万斯曾 称该项目“已经失灵” ，并表示支持取消它。 Mr. Vance said on Thursday that companies like Microsoft had been using the H-1B visa program to exploit the Labor Department’s permanent labor certification program, known as PERM, which allows H-1B visa recipients to obtain a green card and potentially stay in the United States indefinitely. 万斯周四说，微软等公司一直在利用H-1B签证项目，滥用劳工部的永久劳工认证项目(PERM)，该项目允许H-1B签证持有者获得绿卡，从而有可能无限期留在美国。 Officials said that other companies suspended from PERM would include Adobe and several large information technology outsourcing firms. Mr. Vance said the suspension would “last as long as it needs to.” 官员们表示，其他被暂停使用PERM项目的企业还包括Adobe和几家大型信息技术外包公司。万斯说，暂停措施将“持续到不需要为止”。 The announcement on Thursday, which included officials from several agencies, was the latest attempt by the administration to seize on purported fraud to argue that exploitation of the country’s immigration system — and not President Trump’s policies — has been depriving Americans of jobs, wages and paths to prosperity. 多个机构的官员出席了周四的发布会。这是本届政府最新一次试图利用所谓的欺诈行为来辩称，是美国移民制度的漏洞——而不是特朗普总统的政策——剥夺了美国人的工作、工资和致富之路。 “The Department of Labor is taking historic action by shutting down the pipeline of systemic fraud, the fraud that has flooded our country with foreign labor at the expense of American workers,” said Keith Sonderling, the labor secretary. “It begins with universities and companies that have turned into visa mills, promoting foreign workers that have lied about their qualifications to take jobs from our beloved American workers.” “劳工部正在采取历史性行动，切断系统性欺诈的渠道。正是这种欺诈让外国劳动力大量涌入我国，损害了美国就业者的利益，”劳工部长基思·桑德林说。“我们首先要针对那些沦为签证工厂的大学和企业。它们帮助谎报资历的外国员工获得签证，让他们抢走我们亲爱的美国就业者的工作。” But the administration has not always provided evidence to match its fraud claims. And several of its targets on Thursday disputed its assertions. 但特朗普政府提出欺诈指控时，并非总能拿出相应证据。周四被针对的几家机构也对政府的说法提出了异议。 Mr. Vance directed his harshest criticism at Microsoft, saying that there had been “no company in the United States, unfortunately, that has abused this system more.” 万斯对微软的批评最为严厉。他说，“遗憾的是，美国没有哪家公司比它更严重地滥用了这一制度”。 Mr. Vance said that in the past year, the company had laid off 6,000 American workers, while it benefited from 6,300 H-1B visas and nearly 3,000 green cards. He referred to the visa holders as “indentured servants” who were paid a fraction of what their American counterparts would be. 万斯说，过去一年，该公司裁掉了6000名美国就业者，同时却受益于6300份H-1B签证和近3000张绿卡。他把这些签证持有者称为“契约劳工”，说他们的薪酬远低于同等岗位的美国人。 “In other words, if you do the math, for every worker that Microsoft laid off, they replaced that worker with one and a half foreign indentured servants,” Mr. Vance said. “Now that is a scandalous system that we’ve allowed in this country for far too long.” “换句话说，你们可以算一算，微软每裁掉一名员工，就用一个半外国契约劳工来取代他，”万斯说。“这是一个可耻的制度，我们国家容忍它已经太久了。” “And so our message to Microsoft is: You’re a great American company, but you’ve got to hire great American workers,” he added. “You cannot lay off American workers and then replace them with foreign indentured servants.” “所以，我们要向微软传达的信息是：你们是一家伟大的美国公司，但你们必须雇用优秀的美国就业者，”他接着说。“你们不能先裁掉美国就业者，再用外国契约劳工取代他们。” In a statement , Microsoft challenged some of Mr. Vance’s claims. 微软在 声明 中反驳了万斯的部分说法。 The company said the “vast majority” of its employees in the United States are citizens. It said that of the roughly 6,000 H-1B applications it made last fiscal year, 80 percent were to extend or change the status of existing Microsoft employees. The remaining applications were for people already legally in the country who then joined Microsoft, the company said. 该公司表示，其在美国的员工“绝大多数”是美国公民。微软称，上一财年提交的约6000份H-1B签证申请中，80%是为了延长现有微软员工的签证有效期或变更其身份。公司表示，其余申请涉及的也是已经合法身在美国、随后加入微软的人员。 “They are not new arrivals to our country,” it added. “他们并不是新近来到我国的人，”微软补充道。 Microsoft said its pay is among the highest in tech and among H-1B filings. 微软表示，其薪酬水平在科技行业以及提交H-1B签证申请的企业中均位居前列。 “Microsoft succeeds as a global technology leader by developing the world’s best technology work force,” the company said. “We do this by strengthening this country’s talent pipeline, hiring American workers and attracting the best talent from around the world.” “微软之所以能够成为全球科技行业的领导者，是因为我们致力于打造世界一流的科技人才队伍，”该公司表示。“为此，我们不断加强美国本土的人才培养体系，雇用美国工人，同时吸引来自世界各地的顶尖人才。” On the academic front, Mr. Vance maintained that universities were employing foreign graduate students as research assistants at lower wages, and suggested that the visas were being overused and sucking up federal funding. 关于学界方面，万斯坚持认为，大学以较低工资雇用外国研究生担任研究助理，并暗示相关签证被过度使用，消耗了联邦资金。 Anthony D’Esposito, the inspector general of the Labor Department, announced that the agency was launching investigations into several universities for potential abuses of the J-1 visa, a cultural exchange program that allows foreign students to work and study in the United States. 劳工部监察长安东尼·德埃斯波西托宣布，该部门正对多所大学是否滥用J-1签证展开调查。这是一项文化交流签证计划，允许外国学生在美国工作和学习。 “Subpoenas have been served, investigations are underway, and nobody will be getting a free pass because their name is carved into an expensive building,” he said. “传票已经送达，调查正在进行，没有人会因为自己的名字刻在一栋昂贵的大楼上而获得特殊待遇，”他说。 The schools under investigation are Harvard, Yale, Stanford, Arizona State, Brown, M.I.T., the University of Pittsburgh, the University of California, Davis, and the California Institute of Technology. 接受调查的学校包括哈佛、耶鲁、斯坦福、亚利桑那州立、布朗、麻省理工、匹兹堡大学、加州大学戴维斯分校和加州理工。 Stanford said in a statement that it “complies with all applicable visa laws, including those relating to J-1 visas,” and “will cooperate with the investigation.” 斯坦福在声明中说，该校“遵守所有适用的签证法律，包括与J-1签证相关的法律”，并将“配合调查”。 Brian Clark, a spokesman for Brown University, said in a statement that the university had received the subpoena “for various records pertaining to foreign labor programs administered by the U.S. government, and we will respond promptly and directly.” 布朗大学发言人布莱恩·克拉克在声明中说，该校已收到传票，“要求提供与美国政府管理的外国就业者项目有关的各种记录，我们将迅速、直接地作出回应。” “Brown’s international scholars, students and employees make essential contributions on our campus, including to teaching and research that advances American innovation, competitiveness and economic vitality,” Mr. Clark said. “布朗大学的国际学者、学生和员工为我们的校园作出了不可或缺的贡献，包括通过教学和研究推动美国的创新、竞争力和经济活力，”克拉克说。 Arizona State University, noting that it educates more science, technology, engineering and math majors than any other university and employs one of the largest technical and scientific workforces in the country, said that it “has hired the talent needed to perform these functions and done so in complete compliance with existing United States policy and law.” 亚利桑那州立大学指出，该校培养的科学、技术、工程和数学专业学生人数超过美国其他大学，而且拥有全美规模最大的技术和科研人才队伍之一。该校表示，它“聘用了履行这些职能所需的人才，而且完全遵守美国现行政策和法律”。 The H-1B program has long been the target of bipartisan calls for changes, but has become a centerpiece of Mr. Trump’s immigration crackdown agenda. Economists have maintained that the visa holders boost American productivity and raise wages even for American workers. 长期以来，美国两党都呼吁改革H-1B签证计划，但如今它已成为特朗普收紧移民政策议程的核心内容之一。经济学家一直认为，H-1B签证持有人 提高了美国的生产率 ，甚至能够提高美国就业者的工资。 Mr. Vance, pressed on how the use of the certification program amounted to fraud, said that companies were misrepresenting that they were bringing in workers with “hyper-specialized and hyper-capable” skill sets. 当被追问企业使用永久劳工认证制度为何构成欺诈时，万斯表示，企业虚假宣称自己引进的是拥有“高度专业化、能力超群”技能的人才。 Mr. Vance said that there was a difference between bringing in foreign workers like the tech tycoon Elon Musk, “who wants to come in and build something great in the United States of America,” versus an accountant at a lower wage. 万斯说，引进像科技大亨埃隆·马斯克这样“希望来到美利坚合众国成就一番伟业”的外国人才与雇用一名工资较低的会计师是两回事。 “You’re not bringing in a genius to build a great American corporation,” Mr. Vance said. “You are committing fraud against the American people and against this visa program.” “你引进的并不是一个能打造伟大美国企业的天才，”万斯说。“你是在欺骗美国人民，也是在欺骗这一签证项目。” Hours after the announcement, President Trump awarded Satya Nadella, Microsoft’s chief executive, the National Medal of Technology and Innovation at a summit in Washington where Mr. Musk and other tech executives also were honored. 就在这一消息宣布数小时后，特朗普总统在华盛顿举行的一场峰会上向微软首席执行官萨蒂亚·纳德拉颁发了国家技术与创新奖章。马斯克和其他科技企业高管也在会上受到表彰。 Mr. Nadella came to the United States for graduate school and joined Microsoft in 1992. Two years later, he wrote in his memoir, he turned in his permanent residency for an H-1B visa so that his wife could immediately join him in the United States. (At the time, he said, the spouses of green card holders faced a long wait for visa approval.) Both eventually gained citizenship, and he rose through the ranks to revive Microsoft from a yearslong slump. It is now worth almost $4 trillion. 纳德拉来美国读研究生，并于1992年加入微软。他在回忆录中写道，两年后，为了让妻子能够立即赴美与他团聚， 他放弃了自己的永久居民身份，转而申请H-1B签证 。（他说，当时绿卡持有人的配偶需要等待很长时间才能获得签证批准。）两人最终都获得了公民身份，而他也一路晋升，把微软从多年低迷中拯救出来。微软如今市值近4万亿美元。 In awarding Mr. Nadella the highest honor in technology on Thursday, Mr. Trump said it was “so well deserved,” and that Mr. Nadella had turned Microsoft into “an early leader in superintelligence.” 周四，特朗普向纳德拉颁发科技领域最高荣誉时表示，他“完全当之无愧”，并称纳德拉已将微软打造为“超级智能领域的早期领军者”。 Karen Weise自西雅图、Alan Blinder自亚特兰大、Vimal Patel自丹佛、Mark Arsenault自波士顿对本文有报道贡献。 Erica L. Green 是时报白宫记者，报道特朗普总统及其政府。 翻译：纽约时报中文网 点击查看本文英文版。

items.title: AI无处不在：中国面临过度依赖人工智能的挑战
items.description: YAN ZHUANG2026年10月9日中国政府正在对人工智能应用和聊天机器人的使用实施监管，原因是担心该技术可能会干扰人际关系并破坏社会秩序。 Kevin Frayer/Getty Images As China’s government pushes its citizens to embrace artificial intelligence, it is confronting a problem partly of its own making: overreliance on the technology. 随着中国政府推动国民接受人工智能，它正面临着一个部分由自身造成的问题：对这项技术的过度依赖。 State media reports have featured stories that serve as cautionary tales: a farmer who lost 25 acres of seedlings after asking an A.I. for advice, children who have become so attached to chatbots that they want their parents to speak like them and A.I.-generated micro dramas with characters that look like carbon copies of one another. 官方媒体的报道刊登了一些警示案例：一名农民在向人工智能寻求建议后损失了150亩的幼苗；孩子们对聊天机器人过于依恋，甚至希望父母也像机器人那样说话；还有人工智能生成的短剧，其中的角色看起来几乎如出一辙。 These cases and others have raised concerns in China that as it rushes to catch up with the United States in A.I., it is running into adverse side effects created by the new technology, which is accused of undermining human relationships and depriving people of their better judgment. The government, seeking to direct how people use the technology, has responded by imposing new regulations and judicial guidelines on its use — and misuse. 这些案例及其他类似情况在中国引发了担忧，当中国争分夺秒地追赶美国在人工智能领域的步伐时，也遭遇了这项新技术带来的负面影响，人工智能技术被指责破坏人际关系并剥夺人们的判断力。为引导民众正确使用这项技术，政府已针对其使用及滥用行为出台了新的法规和司法指导方针。 The response reflects how the ruling Communist Party is trying to balance its ambitions to promote the widespread use of A.I. with a desire to avoid anything that might undermine social order, say analysts. 分析人士指出，这样的回应反映出，执政的共产党正试图在推动人工智能广泛应用的雄心与避免可能破坏社会秩序的因素之间取得平衡。 The party is “recognizing that the more they develop the technology, the more there’s going to be social challenges that they have to deal with,” said Scott Singer, a fellow and co-director of the China A.I. Initiative at the Carnegie Endowment for International Peace. “Where the party is sensitive is any area where they feel like the technology is getting better in a way that fundamentally could disrupt social stability.” 卡内基国际和平基金会中国人工智能倡议研究员兼联合主任史考特·辛格表示，中共“认识到这项技术发展得越快，他们就越需要应对更多的社会挑战”。“中共特别关注的是那些他们认为技术进步可能从根本上破坏社会稳定的领域。” Mr. Singer said the party is particularly sensitive to disruptions caused not only to human relationships but also the job market as A.I. threatens to replace workers. 辛格表示，随着人工智能威胁取代劳动者，中共不仅对人际关系受到的冲击特别敏感，而且对就业市场受到的破坏也特别敏感。 9月在北京举行的PT博览会上展出的类人伴侣机器人。随着中国面临历史最低出生率的困境，虚拟伴侣应用的兴起引发了人们对人工智能可能取代人际关系的担忧。 Concerns about overuse are shared among China’s citizens, who say they see the spread of the technology as inevitable even as they question its benefits and tire of its ubiquity. 中国民众也普遍担心人工智能被过度使用，他们认为该技术的普及不可避免，但同时也对其效益存疑，并对它无处不在的现象感到厌倦。 Xie Tong, a graphic designer in Beijing, uses A.I. in her own work at a consulting agency and can no longer imagine her life without it. But she despairs at encountering A.I. all around her — in the subway ads that she sees on her commute and in the work of contractors at her job who obviously relied on A.I. 谢彤（音）是北京一家咨询公司的平面设计师，她在自己的工作中使用人工智能，已经无法想象没有它的生活。但对于身边随处可见的人工智能——无论是通勤途中看到的地铁广告，还是工作中那些显然依赖人工智能的承包商的作品——她感到绝望。 “It’s like a marriage where you curse your partner but you can’t leave them,” she said. “就有点像那种你跟一个人结婚，你边骂他，但是你又离不了他那种感觉，”她说。 Limits on Virtual Friends 对虚拟朋友的限制 For a time, China’s A.I. push created a boom in virtual companion apps, including ones offering romantic partners, personal tutors and A.I. avatars of family members. 有一段时间，中国对人工智能的推动引发了虚拟伴侣应用软件的繁荣，其中包括提供恋爱伴侣、个人导师和家庭成员人工智能化身的应用。 In a country already struggling with a shrinking population and a historically low birthrate, the proliferation has led to concerns from Beijing about A.I. replacing human relationships. State media quoted experts saying people could soon find it hard to navigate real interactions. Reports cited a 2025 survey by the China Youth and Children Research Center of more than 8,500 minors that showed more than 20 percent “only wanted to chat with A.I. and did not want to talk with real people.” 在一个正面临人口减少和历史最低出生率困境的国家，这种泛滥引发了北京对人工智能取代人际关系的担忧。官方媒体援引专家的话称，人们可能很快就会发现，难以应对现实中的社交互动。报道引用了中国青少年研究中心2025年对8500多名未成年人进行的一项调查，结果显示，超过20%的受访者“只想和AI聊天，不想和真人聊天”。 That mirrored the concerns of some parents like Vivian Lyu, a stay-at-home mother in Hangzhou who two years ago introduced her 5-year-old daughter, Polly, to Doubao, an A.I. assistant created by ByteDance, the parent company of TikTok. 这反映了一些父母的担忧，比如杭州的全职妈妈维维安·吕（音），两年前，她让五岁的女儿波莉开始使用豆包——一款由TikTok母公司字节跳动开发的人工智能助手。 今年2月，在北京首都国际机场，一则宣传字节跳动人工智能工具的广告。中国政府如今要求，若用户对人工智能伴侣表现出不健康的依赖，相关平台必须予以干预。 Soon, the child was chatting with the A.I. and a personalized companion on the app nearly every day. At first, Ms. Lyu thought the A.I. was good at keeping Polly entertained when the mother had to take care of household tasks. “When you feel like you don’t have a choice, you use Doubao,” she said. 很快，孩子几乎每天都在该应用上与人工智能和个性化伴侣聊天。起初，维维安·吕认为当她需要料理家务时，人工智能可以让波莉解闷。“那没得选择情况下就是我给一个豆包，”她说。 Over time, though, Polly started asking for Doubao instead of seeking out activities that used to interest her, like playing with other children or drawing pictures. Ms. Lyu said she worried that the chatbot was warping her daughter’s understanding of how relationships worked, saying that Polly sometimes talked to Doubao in a “very self-centered, doing-whatever-she-wants kind of way.” 然而，随着时间的推移，波莉开始主动要求使用豆包，而不是去从事她以前感兴趣的活动，比如和其他孩子玩耍或画画。维维安·吕表示，她担心聊天机器人会扭曲女儿对人际关系运行方式的理解，她说，波莉有时以一种“完全以她自我为中心、想怎么样就怎么样的方式”与豆包交谈。 In July, the government imposed limits on A.I. companions that require platforms to step in if users exhibited unhealthy dependencies. Under the new rules, platforms must intervene if users show signs of self-harm. 今年7月，政府对人工智能伴侣施加限制，要求平台在用户表现出不健康依赖时予以干预。根据新规，如果用户表现出自残迹象，平台必须进行干预。 The rules also banned virtual relationships between chatbots and minors, which forced ByteDance to shut down the feature on Doubao that allowed users to create companions. 规则还禁止聊天机器人与未成年人建立虚拟恋爱关系，这迫使字节跳动关闭了豆包上允许用户创建虚拟伴侣的功能。 Polly can no longer access her personalized A.I. companion, but she is still talking to Doubao’s A.I. chatbot, Ms. Lyu said. The mother considered banning her daughter from using chatbots but concluded that such a step could make it harder for Polly to adjust to the technology as she grows older. Instead, Ms. Lyu has limited Polly’s chatbot time to one hour a day. 维维安·吕说，波莉现在无法再使用她个性化的人工智能伴侣，但她仍在与豆包的人工智能聊天机器人对话。她曾考虑禁止女儿使用聊天机器人，但最终得出结论，这样做可能会使波莉长大后更难适应这项技术。因此，维维安·吕将波莉使用聊天机器人的时间限制在每天一小时。 “My hope is for her to understand from a young age that these electronic products, or all of these things related to A.I., are just tools,” Ms. Lyu said. “我比较希望从小时候就让她能感受到，就是说这些电子产品，或者说你所有的AI这些东西只是一个工具，”维维安·吕说。 Real World Problems 现实世界的问题 Just as in many countries, China is struggling with so-called A.I. literacy — understanding how the technology works and its limits. In recent months, the media has documented a growing number of A.I. mishaps involving people who blindly believed in the technology. 和许多国家一样，中国也在应对所谓的“人工智能素养”问题，也就是理解这项技术的工作原理及其局限性。近几个月来，媒体报道了越来越多因盲目相信该技术而引发的人工智能事故。 There was the case of a hiker who became stranded atop a mountain in August after A.I.-generated instructions left him improperly equipped. In several separate cases earlier in the summer, people fell ill after eating poisonous mushrooms that were misidentified by A.I., including a 9-year-old boy who spent eight days in a hospital. 今年8月，一名徒步旅行者因遵循人工智能生成的指南而装备不足，被困在山顶。今年夏天早些时候，还发生了多起因食用被人工智能误识的毒蘑菇而致病的情况，其中一名九岁男孩在医院住院八天。 One of the most widely covered cases involved a farmer in the eastern province of Anhui who lost 25 acres of sesame seedlings in July after following a pesticide regimen drawn up by an A.I. assistant. 最受关注的案例之一发生在东部的安徽省，由于遵循人工智能助手制定的农药施用方案，一名农民7月损失了150亩的芝麻幼苗。 The 67-year-old farmer, whom the reports identified only by his last name, Wu, lost 150,000 yuan, or about $22,000, worth of crops after the A.I. recommended an herbicide that turned out to be unsuitable, the reports said. 报道称，这位67岁的农民（报道中仅透露其姓氏为吴）在人工智能推荐了一种后来被证明不适用的除草剂后，损失了价值15万元人民币的农作物。 The Communist Party’s mouthpiece, People’s Daily, argued in a commentary that A.I. in sectors like agriculture should use only information that comes from authoritative sources. 中共官方媒体《人民日报》在一篇评论文章中指出，农业等领域的人工智能应该只使用来自权威渠道的信息。 北京的一家咖啡馆里，一名用户通过中国科技公司百度开发的人工聊天机器人“万话”展示她的虚拟男友。 It also called for farmers to be trained in “critical thinking about A.I. suggestions, helping farmers transform from passive implementers of technology into active participants who can control the tools.” 文章还呼吁对农民进行“对AI建议的批判性思维”的培训，“帮助农民从被动的技术执行者转变为能主动掌控工具的参与者”。 A Backlash Against Cheap A.I. Fodder 对廉价人工智能“饲料”的反感 A.I. has also become ubiquitous in micro dramas, the wildly popular short-form, soapy shows that are made for mobile viewing. In the first eight months of the year, more than 90 percent of the 430,000 micro dramas released in China were generated by A.I., the government said in late September. 人工智能在短剧中也变得无处不在，短剧是一种专为移动端观看而制作、极受欢迎的短篇肥皂剧。政府在9月下旬表示，今年前八个月在中国上映的43万部微短剧中，90%以上是由人工智能生成的。 These dramas can be churned out cheaply in minutes with no cameras, production crews or human performers. But they have come under fire for their low quality and for taking the jobs of humans. 这些短剧无需摄像机、制作人员或真人演员，几分钟内就能以低成本批量生产。但它们因质量低下以及抢走人类的工作受到抨击。 An article in August in Beijing Youth Daily, the official publication of the Communist Youth League, complained that production companies were churning out A.I.-created micro dramas with boring, interchangeable characters. 共青团官方出版物《北京青年报》8月的一篇文章抱怨称，制作公司正在批量生产由人工智能创作的短剧，其中角色单调乏味、千篇一律。 Some influential voices have gone as far as to say they will boycott micro dramas generated entirely by A.I. 一些有影响力的人士甚至表示，他们将抵制完全由人工智能生成的短剧。 Hu Xijin, the former editor of the state-run Global Times, told his 25 million followers on the social media platform Weibo recently that he would not watch such dramas to avoid “filling up our recreational time with cheap A.I. fodder like pig feed.” 国有《环球时报》前总编辑胡锡进最近在社交媒体平台微博上向其2500万粉丝表示，他不会看这类短剧，以避免“拿廉价的AI饲料像喂猪一样填充我们的娱乐时间”。 Siyi Zhao对本文有研究贡献。 Yan Zhuang是时报驻首尔记者，报道突发新闻。 翻译：晋其角 点击查看本文英文版。
items.content: YAN ZHUANG 2026年10月9日 中国政府正在对人工智能应用和聊天机器人的使用实施监管，原因是担心该技术可能会干扰人际关系并破坏社会秩序。 Kevin Frayer/Getty Images As China’s government pushes its citizens to embrace artificial intelligence, it is confronting a problem partly of its own making: overreliance on the technology. 随着中国政府推动国民接受人工智能，它正面临着一个部分由自身造成的问题：对这项技术的过度依赖。 State media reports have featured stories that serve as cautionary tales: a farmer who lost 25 acres of seedlings after asking an A.I. for advice, children who have become so attached to chatbots that they want their parents to speak like them and A.I.-generated micro dramas with characters that look like carbon copies of one another. 官方媒体的报道刊登了一些警示案例：一名农民在向人工智能寻求建议后损失了150亩的幼苗；孩子们对聊天机器人过于依恋，甚至希望父母也像机器人那样说话；还有人工智能生成的短剧，其中的角色看起来几乎如出一辙。 These cases and others have raised concerns in China that as it rushes to catch up with the United States in A.I., it is running into adverse side effects created by the new technology, which is accused of undermining human relationships and depriving people of their better judgment. The government, seeking to direct how people use the technology, has responded by imposing new regulations and judicial guidelines on its use — and misuse. 这些案例及其他类似情况在中国引发了担忧，当中国争分夺秒地追赶美国在人工智能领域的步伐时，也遭遇了这项新技术带来的负面影响，人工智能技术被指责破坏人际关系并剥夺人们的判断力。为引导民众正确使用这项技术，政府已针对其使用及滥用行为出台了新的法规和司法指导方针。 The response reflects how the ruling Communist Party is trying to balance its ambitions to promote the widespread use of A.I. with a desire to avoid anything that might undermine social order, say analysts. 分析人士指出，这样的回应反映出，执政的共产党正试图在推动人工智能广泛应用的雄心与避免可能破坏社会秩序的因素之间取得平衡。 The party is “recognizing that the more they develop the technology, the more there’s going to be social challenges that they have to deal with,” said Scott Singer, a fellow and co-director of the China A.I. Initiative at the Carnegie Endowment for International Peace. “Where the party is sensitive is any area where they feel like the technology is getting better in a way that fundamentally could disrupt social stability.” 卡内基国际和平基金会中国人工智能倡议研究员兼联合主任史考特·辛格表示，中共“认识到这项技术发展得越快，他们就越需要应对更多的社会挑战”。“中共特别关注的是那些他们认为技术进步可能从根本上破坏社会稳定的领域。” Mr. Singer said the party is particularly sensitive to disruptions caused not only to human relationships but also the job market as A.I. threatens to replace workers. 辛格表示，随着人工智能威胁取代劳动者，中共不仅对人际关系受到的冲击特别敏感，而且对就业市场受到的破坏也特别敏感。 9月在北京举行的PT博览会上展出的类人伴侣机器人。随着中国面临历史最低出生率的困境，虚拟伴侣应用的兴起引发了人们对人工智能可能取代人际关系的担忧。 Concerns about overuse are shared among China’s citizens, who say they see the spread of the technology as inevitable even as they question its benefits and tire of its ubiquity. 中国民众也普遍担心人工智能被过度使用，他们认为该技术的普及不可避免，但同时也对其效益存疑，并对它无处不在的现象感到厌倦。 Xie Tong, a graphic designer in Beijing, uses A.I. in her own work at a consulting agency and can no longer imagine her life without it. But she despairs at encountering A.I. all around her — in the subway ads that she sees on her commute and in the work of contractors at her job who obviously relied on A.I. 谢彤（音）是北京一家咨询公司的平面设计师，她在自己的工作中使用人工智能，已经无法想象没有它的生活。但对于身边随处可见的人工智能——无论是通勤途中看到的地铁广告，还是工作中那些显然依赖人工智能的承包商的作品——她感到绝望。 “It’s like a marriage where you curse your partner but you can’t leave them,” she said. “就有点像那种你跟一个人结婚，你边骂他，但是你又离不了他那种感觉，”她说。 Limits on Virtual Friends 对虚拟朋友的限制 For a time, China’s A.I. push created a boom in virtual companion apps, including ones offering romantic partners, personal tutors and A.I. avatars of family members. 有一段时间，中国对人工智能的推动引发了虚拟伴侣应用软件的繁荣，其中包括提供恋爱伴侣、个人导师和家庭成员人工智能化身的应用。 In a country already struggling with a shrinking population and a historically low birthrate, the proliferation has led to concerns from Beijing about A.I. replacing human relationships. State media quoted experts saying people could soon find it hard to navigate real interactions. Reports cited a 2025 survey by the China Youth and Children Research Center of more than 8,500 minors that showed more than 20 percent “only wanted to chat with A.I. and did not want to talk with real people.” 在一个正面临人口减少和历史最低出生率困境的国家，这种泛滥引发了北京对人工智能取代人际关系的担忧。官方媒体援引专家的话称，人们可能很快就会发现，难以应对现实中的社交互动。报道引用了中国青少年研究中心2025年对8500多名未成年人进行的一项调查，结果显示，超过20%的受访者“只想和AI聊天，不想和真人聊天”。 That mirrored the concerns of some parents like Vivian Lyu, a stay-at-home mother in Hangzhou who two years ago introduced her 5-year-old daughter, Polly, to Doubao, an A.I. assistant created by ByteDance, the parent company of TikTok. 这反映了一些父母的担忧，比如杭州的全职妈妈维维安·吕（音），两年前，她让五岁的女儿波莉开始使用豆包——一款由TikTok母公司字节跳动开发的人工智能助手。 今年2月，在北京首都国际机场，一则宣传字节跳动人工智能工具的广告。中国政府如今要求，若用户对人工智能伴侣表现出不健康的依赖，相关平台必须予以干预。 Soon, the child was chatting with the A.I. and a personalized companion on the app nearly every day. At first, Ms. Lyu thought the A.I. was good at keeping Polly entertained when the mother had to take care of household tasks. “When you feel like you don’t have a choice, you use Doubao,” she said. 很快，孩子几乎每天都在该应用上与人工智能和个性化伴侣聊天。起初，维维安·吕认为当她需要料理家务时，人工智能可以让波莉解闷。“那没得选择情况下就是我给一个豆包，”她说。 Over time, though, Polly started asking for Doubao instead of seeking out activities that used to interest her, like playing with other children or drawing pictures. Under the new rules, platforms must intervene if users show signs of self-harm. 今年7月，政府对人工智能伴侣施加限制，要求平台在用户表现出不健康依赖时予以干预。根据新规，如果用户表现出自残迹象，平台必须进行干预。 The rules also banned virtual relationships between chatbots and minors, which forced ByteDance to shut down the feature on Doubao that allowed users to create companions. 规则还禁止聊天机器人与未成年人建立虚拟恋爱关系，这迫使字节跳动关闭了豆包上允许用户创建虚拟伴侣的功能。 Polly can no longer access her personalized A.I. companion, but she is still talking to Doubao’s A.I. chatbot, Ms. Lyu said. The mother considered banning her daughter from using chatbots but concluded that such a step could make it harder for Polly to adjust to the technology as she grows older. Instead, Ms. Lyu has limited Polly’s chatbot time to one hour a day. 维维安·吕说，波莉现在无法再使用她个性化的人工智能伴侣，但她仍在与豆包的人工智能聊天机器人对话。她曾考虑禁止女儿使用聊天机器人，但最终得出结论，这样做可能会使波莉长大后更难适应这项技术。因此，维维安·吕将波莉使用聊天机器人的时间限制在每天一小时。 “My hope is for her to understand from a young age that these electronic products, or all of these things related to A.I., are just tools,” Ms. Lyu said. “我比较希望从小时候就让她能感受到，就是说这些电子产品，或者说你所有的AI这些东西只是一个工具，”维维安·吕说。 Real World Problems 现实世界的问题 Just as in many countries, China is struggling with so-called A.I. literacy — understanding how the technology works and its limits. items.title: 战争造成燃油短缺，俄罗斯人开始拥抱中国电动汽车
items.description: IVAN NECHEPURENKO2026年10月9日6月，莫斯科一处加油站的排队情况。 Pavel Bednyakov/Associated Press Sergei Tselikov, Russia’s leading auto industry expert, has owned more than 20 vehicles, including a Volvo, a Volkswagen and a Range Rover. All had gasoline engines. 谢尔盖·采利科夫是俄罗斯首屈一指的汽车行业专家，拥有超过20辆车，包括沃尔沃、大众和路虎揽胜，全部为汽油发动机。 But in July, as Ukrainian drone strikes against oil refineries left drivers across the country waiting for hours at gas stations, he bought a fully electric Chinese hatchback. He had to act quickly — the price of the car, made by Great Wall Motor, went up by about $2,000 within days as demand surged. 但在7月，乌克兰无人机袭击炼油厂，导致全国司机在加油站排队数小时，于是他买了一辆中国产纯电掀背车。出手一定要快——由于需求激增，这款长城汽车制造的车几天内售价涨了约2000美元（约合人民币13400元）。 “I tried to fill up one of my cars and drove around to five nearby gas stations, but they had only diesel or lower-grade petrol,” he said, referring to the poorer-quality fuels the government has allowed to be sold to address the shortages. “I was just too lazy to stand in line.” “我试着给其中一辆车加油，跑了附近五个加油站，但只有柴油或低标号汽油，”他说，其中的“低标号汽油”是政府为应对短缺而允许销售的劣质燃料。“我只是懒得排队。” As Ukraine increasingly takes the war to Russia, the effects may be most visible on the roads. Since the end of June, Russia’s electric-vehicle market has more than doubled. Most of the E.V.s sold in the country are Chinese, a testament to Moscow’s economic pivot in response to Western wartime sanctions. 随着乌克兰将战火越来越多地引向俄罗斯，其影响在道路上可能最为明显。自6月底以来，俄罗斯电动汽车市场已增长了一倍多。该国销售的电动汽车大多为中国车，也彰显了莫斯科为应对西方战时制裁而进行的经济转向。 莫斯科一家经销商的一辆中国产插电式混合动力汽车。 Russia is playing catch-up. For years, while other nations built out E.V. supply chains and charging infrastructure, Russia looked the other way. Its position as one of the world’s top oil producers used to keep gasoline cheap. Vast distances between major cities meant charging networks were economically unviable without guaranteed demand. And harsh winters required automakers to heavily adapt models to the climate. 俄罗斯正在追赶。多年来，当其他国家建设电动汽车供应链和充电基础设施时，俄罗斯视而不见。作为世界最大石油生产国之一，俄罗斯曾长期保持汽油低价。主要城市之间距离遥远，意味着在没有稳定需求的情况下，充电网络在经济上难以维系。而严酷的冬季也要求汽车制造商大幅调整车型以适应气候。 Now, E.V.s are suddenly a more common sight on Russian roads, particularly in major cities. The number of electric vehicles, including hybrids, sold in the country went from 43,000 in the January-to-August period of 2025 to more than 83,000 over the same period this year, according to the Russian Ministry of Industry and Trade. 如今，电动汽车在俄罗斯道路上突然变得更加常见，尤其是在大城市。据俄罗斯工业和贸易部数据，该国电动汽车（含混合动力车）销量从2025年1月至8月的43000辆增至今年同期的83000多辆。 By the end of September, the share of pure electric vehicles and plug-in hybrids that can run without gas had reached 11.5 percent of the Russian car market, up from about 5 percent at the beginning of the year, according to Avtostat, an auto research agency led by Mr. Tselikov. The E.V. market share in Russia is now slightly higher than in the United States, but it is only a small fraction of the share in China, which is 45 percent. 据采利科夫领导的汽车研究机构Avtostat的数据，截至9月底，纯电车和可不用汽油行驶的插电式混合动力车在俄罗斯汽车市场中的份额已达11.5%，而年初约为5%。俄罗斯电动汽车市场份额目前略高于美国，但离中国的45%还很遥远。 While the E.V. surge in Russia stems from a specific factor — Ukrainian attacks — the shift there is the latest example of how war and supply shocks can quickly transform car-buying decisions. 俄罗斯电动汽车激增源于一个特定因素——乌克兰的袭击——但那里的转变是战争和供应冲击如何迅速改变购车决策的最新例证。 E.V. sales have boomed in other parts of the world because of the U.S.-Israeli war in Iran, which has caused oil and gasoline prices to soar. Globally, E.V.s are on track to account for a record 29 percent of all new car purchases this year, according to the International Energy Agency. 由于美国和以色列在伊朗的战争导致石油和汽油价格飙升，世界其他地区的电动汽车销量激增。据国际能源署数据，全球范围内，电动汽车今年在所有新车购买量中的占比有望达到创纪录的29%。 E.V. sales have risen in more than 90 countries this year, including Brazil, Australia, India and South Korea. The I.E.A. said the energy crisis had “clearly reinforced the case for E.V.s.” 今年，包括巴西、澳大利亚、印度和韩国在内的90多个国家的电动汽车销量有所上升。国际能源署表示，能源危机“显然巩固了电动汽车的地位”。 中国汽车经销商在俄罗斯迅速增多。 In Russia, the fuel shortages are unnerving many Russians who had grown accustomed to the war in Ukraine being only a distant nuisance. They threaten to become a serious political issue for the government. 在俄罗斯，燃料短缺正让许多人感到不安，他们已习惯于乌克兰战争只是遥远的麻烦。这可能成为政府面临的严重政治问题。 On Friday, only 46 percent of gas stations across Russia were selling fuel, according to Gdebenz, a crowdsourced tool that tracks the fuel market. In Moscow, gasoline was available at 53 percent of stations, leading to some lines. In Nizhny Novgorod, a major city east of Moscow, the figure was only 27 percent. 据追踪燃料市场的众包工具Gdebenz的数据，周五，俄罗斯全国仅46%的加油站销售燃料。在莫斯科，53%的加油站有汽油，导致一些地方出现排队的情况。在莫斯科以东的主要城市下诺夫哥罗德，有油加油站的比例仅为27%。 The situation in Moscow was worse in early July and mid-August, when only a quarter of stations had fuel after strikes on refineries that supply the city. 莫斯科的情况在7月初和8月中旬更糟，在供应城市的炼油厂遭袭后，仅有四分之一的加油站有燃料。 At the time, gasoline lines clogged traffic across the capital. Drivers waited hours for gas at stations on the highways connecting Moscow with St. Petersburg, Kazan and the country’s south. President Vladimir V. Putin had opened these roads with great pride over the past decade. 当时，加油排队的车辆堵塞了首都交通。司机们在连接莫斯科与圣彼得堡、喀山和该国南部的高速公路上的加油站等待数小时。这些过去十年开通的道路是弗拉基米尔·V·普京总统引以为傲的工程。 To try to quell the crisis, the government permitted the sale of lower-grade gasoline and diesel. But some cars began to break down after using the lower-quality fuel. 为平息危机，政府允许销售低标号汽油和柴油。但一些汽车在使用劣质燃料后开始出现故障。 As the fuel crisis has continued, E.V. dealerships have been cleared out, and online listings for used electric cars have dwindled. 随着燃料危机持续，电动汽车经销商的库存已被清空，网上在售的二手电动汽车也越来越少。 At a sprawling dealership complex northwest of Moscow, a manager at Evolute, a brand of Russian-assembled electric vehicles based on Chinese designs, said there was no inventory left on the lot and no way to join a waiting list. 在莫斯科西北部一个庞大的经销商综合体，Evolute——一个基于中国设计的俄罗斯组装电动汽车品牌——的一位经理表示，停车场已无库存，而且也无法预订。 The complex houses more than 40 dealerships, most of which used to sell primarily brands from the West, Japan and South Korea. It now has more than 25 Chinese showrooms. 该综合体拥有40多家经销商，其中大多数过去主要销售西方、日本和韩国品牌。现在它有超过25个中国展销厅。 Many Russian car factories used to produce Western brands but were abandoned after the invasion of Ukraine under pressure from Western governments. Most now assemble Chinese cars. 许多俄罗斯汽车工厂过去生产西方品牌，但在入侵乌克兰后因西方政府压力而被废弃。其中大多数现在组装中国汽车。 On Moscow’s streets and in its parking lots, lines have appeared at charging stations, albeit shorter ones. 在莫斯科的街道和停车场，充电站也出现了排队，尽管较短。 Aleksandr, 40, was charging a red Moskvich, an iconic Soviet brand revived using a rebadged Chinese design, one recent day. He said he had to drive around central Moscow to find a working charger with no line. 最近一天，40岁的亚历山大正在给一辆红色的“莫斯科人”充电，这是一个标志性的苏联品牌，通过重新贴牌的中国设计复活。他说他不得不开车绕莫斯科市中心寻找一个没有排队的可用充电桩。 “Overall, the infrastructure is lacking,” Aleksandr said. The Moskvich belonged to his employer, he said, adding that he would never buy an E.V. for himself because of the expense and the lack of charging stations. “总的来说，基础设施缺乏，”亚历山大说。他说这辆“莫斯科人”属于他的雇主，并补充说他自己永远不会买电动汽车，因为费用高且充电站缺乏。 The shift toward making Russia more E.V.-friendly began in 2022, when the government started subsidizing fast-charging stations and grid connections. In 2023, updated codes required E.V. infrastructure for new buildings. The number of public charging stations grew to more than 8,000 this year from fewer than 1,500 in 2022. 俄罗斯转向电动汽车的趋势始于2022年，当时政府开始补贴快速充电站和电网连接。2023年，更新后的规范要求新建筑配备电动汽车基础设施。公共充电站数量从2022年的不到1500个增至今年的8000多个。 Fully electric vehicles have been exempted from the transport tax paid by owners of other vehicles in many Russian regions. In Moscow and other big cities, E.V. drivers do not have to pay parking fees, which can run as high as $9.50 an hour. Russian-made E.V.s are eligible for government subsidies and can use most toll highways free of charge nationwide. 在俄罗斯许多地区，纯电车已免除其他车辆车主需缴纳的运输税。在莫斯科和其他大城市，电动汽车司机无需支付每小时可能高达9.50美元的停车费。俄罗斯制造的电动汽车有资格获得政府补贴，并可在全国范围内免费使用大多数收费高速公路。 由于汽油变得稀缺，一些俄罗斯人现在改用踏板车和电动自行车。 Tselikov said that while the share of fully electric cars had doubled, they remained somewhat unusual in Russia, primarily because of their cost. Hybrid cars, he predicted, will continue to gain market share. 采利科夫说，虽然纯电车份额翻了一番，但它们在俄罗斯仍然有些不同寻常，主要是因为成本。他预测，混合动力汽车将继续获得市场份额。 E.V.s may also face an image barrier in Russia.
